title: Aft Frame Lower Flange — Corrosion Blend-Out and Protective Restoration
abstract: Interim blend-out repair for surface corrosion on the lower flange of an aft fuselage frame, with a thickness budget that limits how many times the same flange may be blended.

sections.purpose: This repair removes surface corrosion from the lower flange of an aft fuselage frame and restores the protective treatment, within a thickness budget that is tracked for the life of the aircraft.
sections.damage_assessment: Clean the flange and examine it under 10x magnification along its full length; corrosion at this position starts under the protective treatment at the fastener heads and is easy to miss when the surface is dirty. Measure the remaining flange thickness at the deepest point of every affected area with the ultrasonic gauge and record each measurement against the flange position. Compare the measurement with the previously recorded value for that position, because the thickness budget is cumulative over the life of the aircraft and a flange that has already been blended twice may have no budget left. Corrosion that has reached a fastener hole, or that leaves less than 88 per cent of nominal thickness, is outside the scope of this repair.
sections.repair_procedure: Mask the adjacent structure and remove the protective treatment locally with the approved non-metallic method. Blend the corroded area out with a fine abrasive, working along the flange rather than across it, and keep the blended region to a smooth dish with a length to depth ratio of at least 20 to 1. Do not use a rotary burr. Measure the remaining thickness at the deepest point after every blending pass and stop as soon as the corrosion product is gone. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the blended area over its full extent. Where the blend reaches the strap IN377498-58 land, extend the inspection over the strap footprint as well. Apply the chemical conversion coating, the primer and the topcoat of the standard practice of ATA 51-20 and let each layer cure fully before the next is applied. Apply the corrosion inhibiting compound over the blended area and 50 mm beyond it in each direction. Record the blend position, the depth removed and the remaining thickness on the aircraft structural record sheet, and update the cumulative budget for that flange position.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of the blended area at every C-check and an ultrasonic thickness measurement at every second C-check. The repair carries no life limit but the cumulative thickness budget is a hard limit: a flange position that reaches 88 per cent of nominal may not be blended again and needs the insert repair or a frame replacement. Report every blend to Aeralis with the position, the depth and the remaining thickness.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Surface corrosion that blends out leaving not less than 88 per cent of nominal flange thickness, cumulative over the life of the aircraft. Corrosion that has reached a fastener hole is not covered. Not more than three blended positions per frame.
